newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Schipol airport welcomes privatisation plans.
newsitem.headline: Schipol airport welcomes privatisation plans.

text.p: Amsterdam's Schiphol airport on Friday welcomed plans for its possible privatisation, saying it would aid the international development of the facility and generate efficiency gains.
The Dutch government currently holds 76 percent of Schiphol, the Netherlands' main international airport. Amsterdam city council owns 22 percent and Rotterdam city council two percent of the airport.
"(Privatisation) is a logical step in the development of airports into independent, commercial enterprises," the airport said in its annual results statement.

"It offers us a greater access to foreign capital and gives us more space to seek international alliances or participations," it said. "It also forms a stimulus for further efficiency improvement of our business."

The Dutch government has yet to take a firm decision on the possible privatisation, the transport ministry said on Wednesday, with discussions continuing at cabinet level. -- Amsterdam newsroom +31 20 504 5000, Fax +31 20 504 5040
